sections.html:
The Washington County recorder works from the courthouse at 205 Putnam Street, Marietta, OH 45750. Call 740-373-6623, extension 2223 or 2225, or fax 740-373-9643. Counter hours are 8:00 am to 4:30 pm, Monday to Friday, with legal holidays excluded.

Every document that conveys or burdens land in the county goes into the recorder's permanent archive, and the filing fees go to the county's general fund. A deed for any parcel, whether the owner lives in Marietta or in Belpre, Beverly or Waterford, ends up at this counter or in its e-recording queue.

Washington County has 27,987 homes and apartments, and about three of every four occupied homes are lived in by their owners. Marietta is the county seat and largest city. River-valley houses in older neighborhoods and rural parcels outside town call for different paperwork, which is why the courthouse offices below matter. For a rural parcel, ask your title company to check the recorded survey and any easements before you list.

Before you sign a listing agreement, gather the previous deed, the parcel number and the most recent tax bill. Those three papers answer most of what the auditor, the recorder and a buyer's title agent will ask. If you inherited the house or took title through a trust, tell the title company at the start, since those transfers use the exempt-class paperwork described below. Allow a few days for recording once the deed is filed, and keep a copy of the recorded deed for your own files.

sections.h2: Which office does what in a sale
sections.html:
The auditor and recorder share the courthouse at 205 Putnam Street and the 740-373-6623 main line, so a seller can finish two stops in one visit.

Washington County courthouse extensions for deed-related tasks
TaskOfficeExtension
Real estate transfersAuditor2124
Property appraisal valueAuditor2141
Report new construction or demolitionAuditor2141
Homestead exemptionsAuditor2123
Tax mapAuditor2161
Recording a deed or mortgageRecorder2223 or 2225

The auditor's site also posts sales reports, and the auditor's counter keeps the same weekday hours as the recorder, 8:00 am to 4:30 pm.

Paper goes to the counter, and electronic filing runs through approved vendors. Corporation Service Company (866-652-0111) and eRecording Partners Network (888-325-3365) both take deeds. Simplifile is also listed, but it cannot be used for deeds.

Expect a document turnaround of three days. Payment errors are handled this way: filings that arrive under the correct fee are returned, and filings over by $5.00 or more are usually returned too, while an overage under $5.00 is sent back in cash. Mailing the exact amount avoids the delay.

For searching, the recorder links to an online records search and a second cloud-based search. A no-charge search is also available at uslandrecords.com.

sections.h2: Recording fees set by Ohio law
sections.html:
Ohio's section 317.32 builds each charge from two equal halves. The opening two pages cost $17 and $17, later pages cost $4 and $4 apiece, and a preservation surcharge is allowed up to $5. Ask the recorder which surcharge figure the county applies, since the statute sets only the cap.

  • A certified copy is $1 plus $1 a page, with the seal at 50 cents plus 50 cents.
  • Plats and maps are charged by the square inch, with a $20 plus $20 minimum.
  • Declarations under the living will and health care power of attorney statutes run $17 to $20 plus the same range again.
  • County land reutilization corporations are exempt from recorder fees.

The conveyance fee is $.40 per $100 of value. That rate fits the statute's two layers: ten cents per hundred under section 319.54 and up to thirty cents more where commissioners adopted a tax under section 322.02. The auditor's website has a conveyance calculator, and extension 2124 handles real estate transfers.

Transfers in an exempt class pay nothing, though the paperwork still names the class. The cases that come up most in family sales:

  • A gift from one spouse to the other, or from a parent to a child.
  • A deed that corrects an earlier one.
  • A transfer made only as security for a loan.
  • A distribution among heirs where no money is paid.
  • A deed placing the house in a trust the owner can revoke.

When a home carries the homestead reduction, the sale also calls for DTE Form 101, a Statement of Conveyance of Homestead Property.

Every parcel is revalued at market once in six years, and the Ohio Tax Commissioner typically orders a statistical adjustment three years later using actual county sales. Appraisal questions go to extension 2141, and the website has a tax estimator and a delinquency report.

Disputes over value go to the county Board of Revision, made up of a county commissioner, the treasurer and the auditor. The complaint form is due by March 31, and hearings usually fall in April and May. Bring an appraisal report or current sales of similar houses in your neighborhood.

  • Homestead. For seniors 65 and over and permanently and totally disabled owners, on form DTE 105A. It shields $25,000 of market value, and owners with a military service disability can shield $50,000.
  • Owner occupancy reduction. A 2 1/2 percent reduction for the home you own and live in, applied for between January 1 and December 31 at no cost.
  • CAUV. Farm value for at least 10 acres of crops, animals or commercial timber, with a one-time $25 filing fee and a yearly renewal. Missing a renewal costs the savings and brings a payback of the previous three years.

The treasurer, at the same courthouse, collects real estate and manufactured home tax. Call 740-373-6623 and choose option 3 and then 2, any weekday from 8:00 am to 4:30 pm. Manufactured and mobile homes must be registered with the auditor within 30 days of placement in the county, and moving one takes a $5 permit.

sections.h2: Steps from signed deed to recorded deed
sections.html:
The usual order for a Washington County seller looks like this.

  • Have the deed drafted by a title company or attorney and notarized.
  • Call extension 2124 and take the deed to the auditor for the statement of value, the conveyance fee and the endorsement.
  • Send the endorsed deed to the recorder with the exact fee, in person or through an approved e-recording vendor.
  • Ask the treasurer for the tax balance so it can be settled at closing.

A cash sale skips the lender's paperwork, but the deed steps are the same. Because the auditor and recorder share one courthouse, you can usually finish both in a single trip if the deed is ready.

faqs.q: What is the Washington County recorder's phone number?
faqs.a: Call 740-373-6623 and ask for extension 2223 or 2225. Visit the courthouse at 205 Putnam Street in Marietta between 8:00 am and 4:30 pm on weekdays.

faqs.q: Can a deed be e-recorded in Washington County?
faqs.a: Yes, through Corporation Service Company or eRecording Partners Network. Simplifile cannot be used to record deeds.

faqs.q: How long does recording take in Washington County?
faqs.a: Plan on three days. Having the auditor's endorsement and the exact fee on the deed keeps the filing from being returned.

faqs.q: What happens if I send the wrong fee to the Washington County recorder?
faqs.a: A short payment is returned. A payment over by $5.00 or more is usually returned as well, and an overage under $5.00 comes back in cash.

faqs.q: Which Washington County office handles a real estate transfer before recording?
faqs.a: The auditor, at extension 2124 off 740-373-6623. The auditor takes the statement of value and the conveyance fee, endorses the deed, and passes it along to the recorder.
